See how this bachelor compares with study options at UCR

This is a pre-produced programme comparison. Your search helped you find the programme; it did not personalize the comparison.

← Back to search

Economie en Bedrijfseconomie at Tilburg University combines economic theory, accounting, finance, business and data analysis. Students choose an Economics or Business Economics specialisation after the common first year. This comparison shows the Dutch-language Bedrijfseconomie route.

The UCR options combine economics with business and data, public institutions and social policy, or practical finance and quantitative methods. Tilburg retains a more specialised accounting and business-economics sequence and a required 12-EC thesis. Shared rows show partial content relationships, not course equivalence.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Bedrijfseconomie; 2026 entrant cohort; Dutch full-time bachelor

The 180 EC include 30 EC of approved mobility, internship or minor study, whose subject remains unspecified. Financiële Administratie is selected from the six permitted 6-EC electives. GROW is zero-credit extracurricular development and is not added to the 180 EC.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Economics and Business Economics at Tilburg University with 3 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Economics, business & data

A broad closest feasible response combining micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, strategy, organisations, marketing, statistics, data, AI and research methods.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Economics, public institutions & social policy

Economic theory and empirical methods examine public spending, distribution, incentives and economic change. Political and legal institutions, civil society and sustainability governance provide concrete ways to investigate how economic choices become public decisions.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Finance, risk & quantitative analysis

Economics and practical financial decision-making are combined with econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and computational planning under uncertainty. Quantitative methods support economic and financial inquiry; they are not specialised asset-pricing or financial-risk courses.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Accounting & Corporate Finance
This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
Close

Business & Economy in the Age of AI
As we enter the “Age of AI,” this course explores AI’s business, managerial, economic, and societal implications. It is designed for UCR students with a strong interest in AI and requires no prior technical background. The course traces AI’s evolution from early research to generative AI, highlighting its capabilities and limits. Through real-world examples and business cases, students analyse AI’s impact on competitiveness, innovation, labour markets, economic growth, inequality, climate change and society. In this context, students critically examine AI governance and ethics, addressing issues such as bias, privacy, and fairness across business functions (e.g. Marketing, HR, Finance), while also exploring corporate governance and regulation more broadly.
Close

Money, Banking & Finance
This course develops practical financial decision-making skills through case studies and real-world applications. Students learn to analyze financial data, assess risks, and make informed investment, budgeting, and business decisions that enhance value, financial security, and long-term planning.
Close

Introduction to Economics
Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
Close

International Macroeconomics
Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.
Close

Microeconomics & Behavior
Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
Close

Public Economics
Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
Close

Econometrics
Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
Close

Behavioral Economics
This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
Close

Consumer Product Design
You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
Close

Marketing & Consumer Engagement
Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer behaviour, brand strategy and responsible customer engagement. Students analyse case studies, develop marketing plans and consider digital and AI-driven changes in marketing.
Close

Strategy & Digital Transformation
The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
Close

Market Research
See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
Close

International Business & Governance
This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.
Close

Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.
Close

Decision-making in AI
Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
Close

Database Management Systems
Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Machine Learning
Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
Close

Introduction to Programming
Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
Close

Mathematical Methods
Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve mathematical problems and apply these techniques in projects drawing on fields such as science, economics and sociology.
Close

Linear Algebra
Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and applications including Fourier series, difference equations and Markov chains.
Close

Advanced Calculus
Extends elementary calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, including complex‑valued functions. Uses computer algebra software to deepen analytical skills for science and data analysis applications.
Close

Probability & Statistics
Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.
Close

Governance of Sustainability
This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
Close

Law, Society & Justice
Law, Society & Justice examines legal, social and normative perspectives on law. Students explore legal systems and fields including constitutional, administrative, criminal and international law, human rights and selected private-law topics. Case law and trial simulations support discussion of law, society and justice.
Close

Comparative Constitutional Law
Comparative Constitutional Law studies constitutional and administrative law through comparison of five legal systems. Students examine how constitutions establish public institutions, define government powers and protect rights and liberties, alongside the relationship between law, democracy and the constitutional state.
Close

Foundations of European Union Law
Introduces the EU legal order. Studies institutions, framework, citizenship and the internal market using problem‑based exercises and guest lectures.
Close

Ethics
Ethics examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, alongside moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Students apply ethical arguments to issues including equality, poverty and wealth, animal rights, future generations, climate change and historical injustice. Papers and presentations develop independent argumentation.
Close

Introduction to Political Philosophy
Introduction to Political Philosophy examines influential Western thinkers from classical antiquity to the present. Students study views of human nature, society and political authority, place theories in their historical settings and compare their arguments and proposed solutions with contemporary political problems.
Close

Foundations of Comparative Politics
Provides analytical tools to compare political systems and democracies. Examines phenomena like democratic backsliding, decline of political parties, rise of populism, media changes, non‑majoritarian institutions and globalization’s impact on domestic politics.
Close

European Union Politics
European Union Politics examines EU actors, institutions and decision-making rules. Students study how state and non-state interests shape policy and conduct group research on a legislative dossier, interest groups and Members of the European Parliament using the EU transparency register.
Close

Introduction to Sociology
Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois, and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class through theoretical approaches and methodologies.
Close

Qualitative Research Methodology
Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
Close

Modern Sociology
Examines the trajectory of sociology within the culture of imperialism and colonial responses. Studies leading social theories and debates about modernity and critically engages with sociological discourses.
Close

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
Examines contemporary sociological debates about civil society through critical tradition, neo‑functionalism and decolonial critiques. Includes research group projects with NGOs or civil society organizations that translate conceptual insights into empirical analysis.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close
